messages:
Alex: FYI — OrbitX just signed an enterprise POC (2 weeks). They want a production-like throughput run during the POC: peak ~500 QPS (chat), avg 120 tokens in, 250 tokens out (370 tokens total avg). Need sizing, reserved GPU recommendation, autoscale plan, and answers for the security questionnaire. POC start Apr 1. Can eng + SRE help?

Tara: Congrats! quick Qs: is the 500 QPS sustained or bursts? what % of requests are chat vs embeddings? what model family are they expecting (13B/70B)?

Alex: Customer says chat 80% / embeddings 20%. Peak profile: sustained 5m bursts at 500 QPS, then valley at 80 QPS. They prefer a 13B quantized model for cost reasons but want fallback to a 70B distilled variant if quality tests fail.

Mike: Rough calc then (ballpark):
```
peak_qps = 500
tokens_per_req = 370
tokens_per_sec = peak_qps * tokens_per_req = 185000 t/s
assume_model_throughput_per_gpu = 50000 t/s (13B quantized, optimistic)
gpus_needed = ceil(185000 / 50000) = 4
```
So steady reserve should be at least 4 GPUs for peak without autoscale. For safety w/ KV cache warmup and headroom, recommend reserved 5 (or reserved 4 + 1 prewarm slot). If they want rolling deploys + canary, keep an extra slot.

Tara: Important nuance: tokens/sec numbers depend a lot on seq length distribution. If many longer responses, throughput per GPU drops ~30%. We should ask for 95th percentile output length. Also KV cache hit-rate affects perf for chat (higher hit-rate → fewer decode tokens).

Alex: I'll ask OrbitX for token length percentiles. For presales though we need a proposal tomorrow. What about autoscale strategy?

Mike: Autoscale suggestion: min_reserved = 3 (keeps baseline), reserved_commit = 4 (monthly contract), burst_slots = 2 (burst credits/autoscale up to 6), scale_step = 1 GPU, cool_down = 90s. Policy: route to reserved pool first; if saturated, fall back to burst pool (pay-as-you-go GPUs). Configure prewarm for warmup of KV cache for top N users (we can preheat prefixes).

Jess: From product/ops POV: we should recommend configuring: prefix caching enabled, aggressive batching for embeddings route, and model-variant fallback with automatic reroute to 70B-distilled only if quality regressions are detected. Also add a queue_depth throttling at 1s latency spike to avoid cascading failures.

Alex: Pricing question from OrbitX: they want delta between reserved vs burst-credit pricing and the cost to keep the extra prewarm slot 24/7. Any numbers we can quote?

Mike: Rough monthly numbers (internal ballpark, to be finalized by finance): reserved_A100_equiv_monthly = $5k-$7k per GPU. Burst/GPU on-demand ~1.6x reserved. Prewarm slot = same as one GPU but prorated hours used. We'll flag these for finance to confirm.

Sam: Security questionnaire items they've flagged: data residency (EU), BAA/HIPAA, KMS integration, SOC2 reports, and fine-grained access controls. We need answers for: where logs live, how long audit logs retained, can we support customer-managed keys, and is there a formal BAA?

Jess: Answers: 1) We can deploy on EU region for data residency. 2) We support customer-managed KMS via our Private offering (on-prem/VPC). 3) SOC2 report available on request. 4) BAA is a legal ask — we need Legal to sign off; typical turnaround 5-10 business days.

Alex: OrbitX also asked about encryption-in-use / HSM.

Sam: We support KMS/HSM integrations for Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and can arrange customer-managed keys in VPC setups. Note: HSM-backed KMS often requires dedicated network config and procurement lead time.

Tara: Ops follow-up: KV cache warmup strategy — we should recommend: preheat top 100 prefixes, enable persistent KV caching, and run a 12h warmup job before the POC peak day. That will reduce token decoding load by ~20-30% on hot sessions.

Mike: Also recommend a canary rollout: start 10% traffic on day 1 with health monitors (p50/p95/p99 latencies + error rate), then 50% day 2, 100% day 3 if green. Add auto-fallback to smaller model if latency > 1.2x SLA for 5 minutes.

Alex: OrbitX legal asked about retention/PII handling in training data — short answer?

Sam: We do not use customer inputs for model training by default. Data processing is scoped to inference only unless there's an explicit data-sharing contract. We'll put that in writing for the questionnaire.

Alex: Great. Can we get an initial capacity + price + security one-pager by EOD tomorrow for presales? I'll include it in the SOW draft.

Mike: I'll produce a sizing slide + math and run it by infra finance.

Jess: I'll draft ops checklist (preheat steps, canary plan, fallback policies).

Sam: I'll handle security answers and note exceptions for Private/KMS requirements.

infra-bot: deploy-sim: preheat-job scheduled for 2024-04-29T03:00Z for warmup-run (top-100 prefixes).

Alex: Nice — thanks everyone. I'll push the one-pager to the deal doc and loop in finance. :thumbsup:

Mike: quick note — if OrbitX insists on 70B served at peak, multiply GPUs estimate by ~2.5x. Call that out in the one-pager as a high-cost scenario.

Tara: +1 on highlighting sensitivity (seq length, model family, KV hit-rate). We'll include a simple sensitivity table.

Alex: Action items recap (for the thread):
- Mike: sizing slide + cost ranges by model variant (due EOD tomorrow)
- Jess: ops runbook + preheat checklist (draft by tomorrow noon)
- Sam: security questionnaire answers & BAA timeline (24h)
- Alex: finalize SOW + attach one-pager to customer email

Tara: acked.

Mike: acked.

Sam: acked.

Alex: Thanks — will ping again if OrbitX returns any extra asks.
